Something like SCP-1329 is a Foundation SCP document that is about an SPC GOI related anomaly, and therefore should be tagged as an SCP.

Something like SPC-140 is a document made by an SPC GOI so it should be tagged as a GOI format.

This isn't any different from SCP-1637 being a Prometheus Labs project in Foundation containment and tagged scp and prometheus compared to GRANT REQUEST FOR GENETICALLY ENGINEERING LOW-COST ORGANIC AUTOMATONS WITH SOPHISTICATED ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR LABOR being a Prometheus Labs produced document and tagged with goi_format and prometheus.

Does that help?

item.content:encoded:
I'll admit I skimmed over some of the jargon, but I didn't really think it was unreasonably excessive. I think part of why it feels that way might just be because it's different jargon than we're used to.

What was that Bee Obliteration Registry "K"? A whole organization devoted to obliterating bees seems very implausible. /j No but that bit did seem kind of thrown in for no reason. I got the gist of what happened overall but there were several unnecessary parts like that - I feel like large parts of this could be taken out as separate tales.

If I'm understanding the end right, it's implied that the meme responsible for the bird apocalypse was created by the Shark Punching Center?

+1 for that and the Statue of Libirdty. Tempted to no-vote because of the unnecessary length, but eh, I can't really complain when you managed to have the Shark Punching Center cause the apocalypse.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is the first time I've fully read an SPC article and understood the narrative and technical purpose behind the theme, so the satirical technobabble held a certain charm (I'm still getting over how philosophical the name "Centre Pugilists" sounds). I was also fairly amused by the hypocrisy in the exchange with the Bee Obliteration representative, and the subtle call to Planet of the Apes (that I got, at least) with the Statue of Libirdty and the transformation of that civilization. However, I realized (as TL333s did) that I had no idea what the heck was happening when I reached the latter; and found the dialogue forced at times, specifically at the end. It's clear you put a lot of work into this, and it actually captivated me for the first few paragraphs; but, by the time I finished, I felt the concept and execution had fallen flat.

TL;DR: No vote from me.

SPC-001 in-universe is a Selachian threat, just not one they're able to punch.

The Centre's goal is a capability for pugilising the capital-S Selachian, SPC-001. Punching sharks, their mission as a whole, is the Centre's only means of delaying SPC-001's arrival in this universe (a part of some other nonsense known as CASE LIQUID WHITE). Why it's so needlessly complicated is beyond me, but I can assure you, the Centre is more than equipped to pugilise these deviants to hell.

Is it just me, or does it seem like a lot of these SPC format articles are almost impenetrably technical? Like, I get that it's supposed to a satire of traditional SCP tone, and I enjoyed this just fine once I got to the logs, but it was hard to appreciate the silliness of the main document underneath all the jargon.

Also, I almost can't believe I'm making a nitpick like this, but why is it implied that SPC-001 is a selachian threat if the SPC designation system is used for internal projects? Normally I'd be loathe to get hung up on a detail like this in something as silly as the Shark Punching Center, but considering the emphasis this article seems to place on international logic and consistent lore, it seems rather out of place.
